\chapter{Review --- the Two Conditions}
\label{ch:repaso-condiciones}
\hlchaptermodality{209}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can choose between a real and an unreal condition and get both halves right.}

I can choose between a real and an unreal condition and get both halves right.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[the two conditions]{Review — the two conditions}

\label{lesson:ES-C56-repaso-condiciones}



\begin{quote}
Which follows \emph{si} in a real condition? (The \textbf{present}.) In an unreal one? (The \textbf{supposing} form.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Say each one aloud, one after another. They are three sentences about the same afternoon, and only the verbs differ.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Si tengo tiempo, hablo español.} — whenever it happens
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Si tengo tiempo, hablaré español.} — a plan for today
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Si tuviera tiempo, hablaría español.} — but I do not have it
\end{quote}

Notice what \emph{si} itself contributes: \textbf{nothing}. The same three letters open all three. Everything that tells the worlds apart is carried by the verbs standing on either side of it.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the two rules that never bend}]
\textbf{The future never follows \emph{si}.} \emph{Si tendré} is not said. If the result is in the future, the \emph{si} half stays in the present.

\textbf{The present subjunctive never follows \emph{si} either.} \emph{Si tenga} is not said. Supposing after \emph{si} is always the \emph{-ra} form.

Two prohibitions, one word. Everything else about \emph{si} is free.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} the three sentences, in order
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
How many worlds can you now describe? (\textbf{Three} — habitual, planned, and not the case.) What does \emph{si} change between them? (\textbf{Nothing}.) And which two forms may never follow it? (The \textbf{future} and the \textbf{present subjunctive}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
